subject: Post-demo: integration roadmap, rate limits, and SLA questions
messages:
From: Ana Rivera <ana@fulcrumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's demo — hosted vs dedicated questions

Thanks for the demo earlier — really helpful. A couple of follow-ups from the engineering and procurement teams as we think about the pilot:

- Quick context: pilot will be a user-facing summarization feature for our care coordination app. Expected steady-state: ~30 TPS at peak bursts up to ~120 TPS for ~10 minute windows. Typical input sizes ~400 tokens; output ~120 tokens.
- Compliance: we need to understand what data leaves our VPC for hosted evaluation (headers, logs, retention). SOC 2 evidence would be great.
- Performance targets: P95 latency < 350ms for our summary endpoint is a hard ask.
- Cost/ops: do you recommend starting on Hosted API for the pilot or go straight to Dedicated? Our procurement lead prefers hosted to avoid long-term commitments but will need SLA language for uptime and data handling.

Specific asks:
1) From your side, which deployment mode you recommend for an initial 6-week pilot that could scale into production?
2) Do you provide sandbox endpoints and tokens immediately after the call? If so, what are starter rate limits per endpoint?
3) Any short checklist for our engineers to integrate quickly (network egress, auth, sample SDK usage)?

Can we aim to reconvene early next week after you send details?

Thanks,
Ana Rivera
Senior PM, Fulcrum Health
ana@fulcrumhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Rivera <ana@fulcrumhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — hosted vs dedicated questions

Hi Ana — great to meet you on the call. Appreciate the clear context and the traffic profile — that helps a lot. High-level answers below, plus next steps and attachments (onramp checklist + a starter SLA draft).

Short answer and recommendation
- Recommendation: Start with Hosted API for the 6-week pilot. Reasons: fastest time-to-value, immediate sandbox endpoints and tokens, built-in monitoring and fallback variants. Hosted lets you validate latency and quality before committing to Dedicated. If you need committed throughput or strict network isolation later, we can plan a Dedicated reservation or Private VPC in the next phase.

Performance and rate limit guidance (starter plan)
- Sandbox endpoints: sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/summarize and sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/stream-summary - Recommended starter rate limits (can be adjusted during pilot):
  - summarize endpoint: 60 req/s, burst up to 150 req/s (10-minute windows)
  - stream-summary: 30 concurrent streams, 150 token/s aggregate
- Note on latency: P95 < 350ms is achievable for the profile you described if you use the streaming endpoint for short outputs and enable prefix KV cache for repeated prompts. We'll monitor and advise tuning.

Compliance and data handling
- We attach a short onramp checklist that includes data retention defaults for Hosted evaluations (30 days logs, ability to opt-out of logging for pilot data, and support for customer-supplied KMS on Private later). I also attached a starter SLA for procurement to review. For SOC 2 evidence and deeper compliance artifacts, our security team can share a redacted SOC 2 report under an NDA; I can get that thread started if you want.

Integration checklist (attached) — highlights:
- Network: outbound HTTPS only; no inbound ports required.
- Auth: API key per sandbox user; supports short-lived tokens and OAuth for prod flows.
- SDK: node/python examples included — sample-behavior for stream vs batch.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency in Console and webhook hooks for error events.

Next steps
1) I can provision sandbox tokens + endpoints by EOD.
2) If you want, we'll schedule a 30-min integration session with Rishi and one of our solutions engineers to walk through the integration checklist.
3) We'll also ensure Procurement receives the SLA draft and a pointer to compliance artifacts.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-onramp-checklist.pdf, sla-draft-fulcrum.docx

Would Tuesday 9am PT for an integration session work for your engineers?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T15:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — hosted vs dedicated questions (technical notes)

Quick technical notes to include in the integration session agenda:
- Canary routing: suggest mapping a single summarize endpoint to two model variants (gpt-small-fast for early traffic, gpt-medium-fp16 for canary bursts). This lets us meet latency SLO while validating quality.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated user prompts to cut token cost ~20–30% for your workload.
- Seq-length and batching: with ~400-token inputs, we should set batching windows small (20–40ms) to avoid high p95. We'll tune in the sandbox.
- Network considerations: if Fulcrum needs Private later, switching routes is straightforward — same endpoint semantics, just different routing policy.

Link to the HubSpot ticket for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-2028-FH-42

I'll join the Tuesday session if it works — can prep a short checklist and a sample postman collection for your engineers.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick confirmations: 

- Fulcrum is happy to start with Hosted for the pilot provided we get the sandbox tokens and the SLA draft for review by procurement.
- Please send SOC 2 redacted evidence under NDA; procurement will sign an NDA if needed.
- Tuesday 9am PT works for our engineering lead (I'll send a calendar invite). Please include Rishi on the invite so we can go over the canary routing and batching items.

Also: can you include a short example curl and node snippet for the streaming endpoint in the sandbox? That will speed up our integration.

I'll loop procurement on the SLA once we have the doc attached.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the tokens and link to the integration session.

Best,
Ana Rivera
